topics.title: The Prusa CORE One INDX Has Problems
topics.description: Thomas Sanladerer's review: third-party filament fails the mandatory calibration, settings don't save, and the camera is blocked

slides.heading: The Prusa CORE One INDX Has Problems
slides.body: Made with Layers, October 11. 264,000 views in four days, and a Hackaday follow-up on Monday.

slides.heading: What Tom Found
bullets: The mandatory start-of-print calibration only works with Prusa's own filament. VoxelPLA wouldn't print until he deleted the sequence from the G-code by hand
Prusa support's answer: use Prusament. It struggles with some Prusa filaments too
Manual calibration results aren't saved, even though the screen says they are
The INDX hardware blocks the camera, so you can't check a filament load
Side by side, his Prusa XL "simply works." What's good: 0.013 g of purge per change, and the Bondtech extruders

slides.heading: The Pushback, and Where It Stands
bullets: Owners in the comments print third-party filament fine and suspect a firmware or slicer fix since he filmed
One engineer's read: nozzle ooze upsets the force probe, not the filament brand
Others pile on: tool heads flying off during changes, filament locking up in the channels
No response from Prusa yet. Nothing new since firmware 6.9.2 on October 7
Still a beta unit sold as a finished product. Give it two more years

topics.title: Creality K3: Pre-Orders Open at $849
topics.description: Four nozzles, five-second swaps, and the Snapmaker U1's silhouette. Every number is Creality's own

slides.heading: Creality K3: Pre-Orders Open at $849
slides.body: Announced Tuesday, under the sub-$900 promise from last month. Four free rolls of Hyper PLA if you order by November 30.
bullets: KliTek: four nozzle assemblies docked at the back, swapped in about 5 seconds. A full material change in under 15
Creality's claims: up to 85% less waste and up to 80% shorter print times than a single-nozzle multi-color setup
260 mm cube, 500 mm/s, 300 °C hotend, four built-in spool slots, four hardened 0.4 mm nozzles in the box
Klipper-based firmware with root access. Creality Print 7.0, and OrcaSlicer works

slides.heading: Snapmaker Clone? Close, but Not Quite
bullets: Same shape as the Snapmaker U1: four tools, CoreXY, about $850 to $900
The U1 swaps whole toolheads. The K3 swaps lightweight nozzle assemblies. Bambu's H2C swaps hotends. Three answers to the purge-waste problem
Extras cost extra: the mixed-nozzle kit, the TPU kit, the CFS hub for more colors, the filtered top cover. No chamber heater
No US ship date yet. No independent review yet. Europe in December
It's a Creality pre-order. Remember the K2 Plus

topics.title: Formlabs Form Studio 1: Professional Resin for $699
topics.description: Formlabs' first printer aimed at the home desk. Not as cheap as the headline, but affordable

slides.heading: Formlabs Form Studio 1: Professional Resin for $699
slides.body: Announced Wednesday, orders open now, ships November 16. I want one.
bullets: A quarter of the Form 4's price. Formlabs calls it "the world's most affordable professional resin 3D printer"
200 × 125 × 235 mm build volume. New Low Force Display engine from the Form 4: 28 LEDs, 35 µm pixels (30% finer than the Form 4)
Averages 40 mm/h, up to 130 mm/h with Alpha Fast. Most prints under two hours
Founder's Edition colors (aqua, teal, violet) through November 30. One-year warranty

slides.heading: Not As Cheap As You Think
bullets: Six Alpha Resins from $29 per liter. Nine materials supported at launch
Resin tank $55. Tank Pro $79, and you need it for third-party resin (at a speed cost)
Flex build plate $135. Form Studio Wash+Cure $199. The VOC extractor is extra too
Call it $1,000 to $1,100 on the desk before resin. Still the cheapest way into PreForm and Formlabs materials

topics.title: California Sues Polymaker Over "Ghost Gun" Marketing
topics.description: San Diego County says the filament isn't illegal, the marketing is. First suit of its kind

slides.heading: California Sues Polymaker Over "Ghost Gun" Marketing
slides.body: Filed October 5 in San Diego Superior Court by the County Counsel, with Giffords Law Center. The complaint says filament itself is legal.
bullets: The claim: Polymaker's marketing turned PLA into a "firearm precursor part" under California law
Alleged: firearm-themed products, paid affiliates and influencers in the gun-printing scene, technical guidance

slides.heading: What the County Is Asking For
bullets: Named 65 times: Sean Aranda, "The 3D Print General," sponsored by Polymaker and then hired as Head of Customer Experience
Asks for an injunction, civil penalties up to $2,500 per violation, and the profits
No statement from Polymaker yet. Allegations, not findings. We'll follow it

topics.title: 3D-Printed "Hair": A Hairy Combat Robot in 48 Hours
topics.description: Maker's Muse armors an antweight with printed bristles. Same trick makes grass

slides.heading: A Hairy Combat Robot in 48 Hours
slides.body: Maker's Muse, October 7. All his robots were broken the week of Robot Royale 9, so he built a new one with 3D-printed hair.

slides.heading: How You Print Hair (and Grass)
bullets: A 150 g antweight designed in Fusion and printed on an Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2, wired and fought inside two days
The bristles come from the "hairy lion" trick: the slicer bridges each strand to a sacrificial wall, you cut the wall away and the hairs stay
A hair dryer straightens or curls the strands after
Grass works the same way. Print the lawn sideways, one strand per blade from tip to root, then free the plate

topics.title: The Vibe-Coding Era
topics.description: AI made custom software cheap to build. The tools keep coming, this deck included

slides.heading: The Vibe-Coding Era
slides.body: A lot of custom-built software exists now because of what AI can do. This slide deck and our own products included.
bullets: Small, focused tools, built by one person, often in a weekend
Most run in the browser. Nothing to install, nothing uploaded
Several ship an MCP server, so an AI assistant can drive the tool for you
I keep a list on our GitHub and add to it every week as I find more

slides.heading: The List So Far
bullets: CurveCut: a free Luban3D alternative
Printfins: a better way to support models
Layerling: a self-hosted version of Tinkercad
JumpStart 3D: a better version of Tinkercad. I'm hosting it now
SolidCraft: parametric CAD, 2,685 stars in eight days
FluidCAD: parametric CAD you can write as JavaScript
Bumpmesh: textures for your 3D files

slides.body: Six hearts last week. The Yeah Hand and the microplastics filter tied at two each, so the robot hand takes the spot.
bullets: Vittorio Lumare's open-source robot hand: 5 servos, 15 degrees of freedom, fishing-line tendons, mostly printed

Runner-up: the PLA-plus-PEG filter that catches about 90% of microplastics

topics.title: Robotics Corner: Gemini 4 Argon Teaches a Humanoid Cornhole
topics.description: Google's new model watched one video, wrote the simulation, and Apptronik's Apollo sank seven in a row

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: Gemini 4 Argon
slides.body: Google DeepMind, October 13. Argon is Google's new general model; robotics is one showcase.

slides.heading: Video to Sim to Real
bullets: Researchers showed Argon a video of a person playing cornhole. It mapped the scene and built a MuJoCo physics simulation on its own
The control it worked out ran on Apptronik's Apollo humanoid: seven consecutive shots in the real world
Google says the pipeline compresses weeks of manual simulation modeling into a few hours
Also shown: Spot rehearsing a foot-pedal trash bin in a digital twin, and a $100-class SO-101 arm
Not open and not free: paid API or a Google AI Pro/Ultra plan. All numbers are Google's own, from an internal test

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: Support Fins, Three Weeks Later
topics.description: Matthew Trahan's breakaway-fin tool went from 455 to 750 stars, grew plugins for seven apps, and became an MCP server today

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: Support Fins, Three Weeks Later
slides.body: Our W39 Quick Tip, revisited. Matthew Trahan's free web app bakes breakaway fins into your STL so the stronger orientation prints. I'm still talking with Matthew and contributing.
bullets: 455 stars when we showed it on September 24. 750 today, 10 contributors, about 200 commits in three weeks
Plugins now: OrcaSlicer, PrusaSlicer 3.0, Cura 5, Fusion, Blender 4.2+, FreeCAD 1.0, Onshape, SolidWorks. All marked experimental
A command line that fins a part with one command, and a Portuguese translation from a contributor

slides.heading: What Landed This Week
bullets: Support Fins as an MCP server, published today. Claude Code or Claude Desktop can fin a part for you
Orientation suggestions moved to a background worker. A 250,000-face model used to freeze the page for 14 seconds
A bed pad on exports, cutouts along cut walls, and calibration coupons you print to tune the fins to your printer
Still free, MIT, nothing uploaded. The fin idea is Slant 3D's; Matthew automated it

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Thermoform PLA: print it flat, press it over a mold with a hair dryer

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Thermoforming PLA
slides.body: Send to Print, October 10. Flat PLA mesh panels, a reusable PETG mold, and a hair dryer make a ghost treat bag you couldn't print directly.

slides.heading: How Thermoforming Works
bullets: Print the panels flat in PLA. Print the forming mold in PETG, which holds up to the heat
Warm the PLA with a hair dryer or heat gun until it goes limp, press it over the mold, let it cool
Lighter and faster than printing the shape, and the mold is reusable
Free files on MakerWorld: ghost, candy corn and cloud treat bags in two sizes. The Fusion tutorial covers the hinge, threads and cap
